assertion: In Los Angeles, the tide peaked at 8.19 feet above the average low tide, tying the record set just last month.
warehouse_value: max 2.49 m = 8.17 ft through 2026-10-31 (high_low product); NOAA water_level Nov 25 max 8.194 ft (preliminary)
sql: SELECT station_id, MAX(water_level_m)*3.28084 FROM weather.coops_high_low WHERE station_id IN ('9410660','9410230') AND event_date<='2026-10-31' GROUP BY station_id
measure: Los Angeles tide gauge record water level November 2026

assertion: In La Jolla, waves smashed into houses, also breaking the high tide record just a month after it had been set.

assertion: In 2024, Long Beach put a $125 million project to retrofit the area's aging sea walls on hold briefly when the price tag of the first two phases ballooned.
inaccuracy: The claim says the hold was brief and followed ballooning costs of the first two phases; the Long Beach Post piece says the city needs $125M to finish the 86-year-old wall and cites an anticipated oil-revenue decline, with no mention of ballooning costs or a brief hold; LAist says officials halted reconstruction.
independent_value: LB Post: city needs $125M; LAist: officials halted reconstruction citing oil revenue and disaster aid
searched: Long Beach Naples seawall $125 million on hold 2024

assertion: An anticipated steep decline in the area's oil production left the Tidelands Operations Fund with a severe budget deficit, according to local officials.
reason: The LB Post page ICN links says oil restrictions could cost the city up to $20M/yr and projects a $23.5M general budget deficit, but never mentions the Tidelands Operations Fund; no page found states a Tidelands fund deficit.
searched: Long Beach Naples seawall Tidelands Operations Fund deficit
measure: Long Beach Tidelands Operations Fund deficit
why_no_page: No page stating a Tidelands fund deficit was found; the page ICN links was read and does not mention the fund.

assertion: I do think we're seeing more king tides, more extreme tides, than we did back in the early 2000s. So, you're getting these 7-plus footers more than we did back then.
speaker: Craig Auger
reason: Direction supported: LA highs of 7 ft or more averaged 13.5/yr in 2010-2019, 16.3/yr in 2020-2025, 41 in 2026 to date. Warehouse starts 2010, so the early-2000s baseline itself is untested, and the gauge is LA not Newport Beach.
sql: SELECT year, COUNT(*) FROM weather.coops_high_low WHERE station_id='9410660' AND event_type IN ('H','HH') AND water_level_m*3.28084>=7.0 GROUP BY year ORDER BY year
measure: Newport Beach high tide 7 feet frequency by year
independent_value: weather.com: records topped in Oct and Nov 2026
